---
title: "Troubleshooting"
---

## Common Issues

| Problem | Likely cause | Solution |
|---|---|---|
| No PNG files appear on the display | USB flash drive detected but not mounted | Mount `/dev/sda1` in `/mnt/pattern_usb` |
| ESP32 is not detected | Wrong serial device selected | List ports and use `/dev/ttyUSB0` when available |
| `lcd.contrast()` error | Installed `gfxhat` library has no `contrast()` method | Guard the call with `hasattr(lcd, "contrast")` |
| Arduino compilation reports `redefinition` | Two complete `.ino` files are in the same sketch folder | Put `servo_switch_usb.ino` in its own folder |
| Servos do not move | External 5 V supply is off or wiring is incomplete | Verify DC-DC supply, signal pins and common ground |
| Microswitch does not generate advancement | Connected to `NC` or wrong GPIO | Use `COM → GND`, `NO → GPIO25` |
| Display works but progress does not increase | No `NEXT` message received from ESP32 | Check microswitch and USB serial connection |

## USB Flash Drive Not Visible

Check the storage device:

```bash
lsblk -o NAME,SIZE,FSTYPE,LABEL,MOUNTPOINTS,MODEL
```

In the tested setup, the pattern flash drive appears as:

```text
/dev/sda1
```

If no mount point is shown, mount it:

```bash
sudo mkdir -p /mnt/pattern_usb
sudo mount /dev/sda1 /mnt/pattern_usb
ls -lah /mnt/pattern_usb
```

The PNG files must be directly inside `/mnt/pattern_usb`.

## ESP32 Serial Port

List serial devices:

```bash
python3 -m serial.tools.list_ports -v
```

The tested ESP32 CP2102 bridge appears as:

```text
/dev/ttyUSB0
```

Use it when launching the interface:

```bash
python3 /home/aless/gfxhat_pattern_ui_usb.py --usb-dir /mnt/pattern_usb --port /dev/ttyUSB0
```

## GFX HAT Contrast Compatibility

If the program stops with:

```text
AttributeError: module 'gfxhat.lcd' has no attribute 'contrast'
```

replace the unconditional call with:

```python
lcd.clear()
if hasattr(lcd, "contrast"):
    lcd.contrast(42)
self.set_backlight((0, 40, 70))
```

## Arduino Redefinition Error

Each Arduino sketch must be placed in its own directory:

```text
servo_switch_usb/
└── servo_switch_usb.ino
```

Do not keep the former firmware `.ino` in the same directory as the new USB-controlled sketch.
